title: The Attack by Fire
coreMove: Use volatile force only when timing, materials, wind, and advantage line up, because damage cannot be called back.
sourcePressure: The source names five fire attacks, insists on ready materials, dry weather, special wind days, five developments after fire starts, windward position, signal fires, and restraint against anger or pique.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reading fire as aggression, escalation, or dramatic action rather than controlled irreversible force.
sourceAlignmentTerms: five ways of attacking with fire

sourceAnchors.name: the constellations of the Sieve, the Wall, the Wing, and the Cross-bar
sourceAnchors.detail: The source links special days for fire to these constellations because they are days of rising wind.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Fire strategy begins by looking up: not every dry day has the wind for irreversible action.

sourceAnchors.name: signal-fires and drums
sourceAnchors.detail: Night operations rely on signal-fires and drums, while day fighting relies mainly on banners and flags.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Once conditions turn volatile, the signal system matters as much as the spark.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
